University Prestige and Source Credibility: Moderating Roles for Need for Cognition and Trust in Science and Scientists

PSY 120L Reproducible Analysis Report

Author

Peter Mirich

# About This Report

About This Report

This reproducible report documents the data preparation, variable construction, descriptive statistics, primary analyses, and figures for this study.

The report is intended to accompany a manuscript-style research paper. It is not the full paper itself. Instead, it shows how the reported analyses were produced from the dataset using a transparent and reproducible Quarto workflow.

Study Overview

This study examined whether a university’s name influenced perceived credibility of the university’s research on a health topic, and whether credibility ratings differed by need for cognition (NFC), trust in science and scientists (TIS), and their interactions with university prestige.

Two 2 x 2 between-subjects factorial ANOVAs used university prestige as the manipulated independent variable in both analyses. Each ANOVA manipulated a different categorical moderator:

  • Need for Cognition:  high versus low

  • Trust in Science and Scientists:  high versus low.

The dependent variable was the perceived source credibility rating.

The primary analyses tested whether the main effect of university prestige and the particular moderators, NFC or TIS, and whether each moderator’s interaction with university prestige, predicted each source credibility outcome.

Setup and Software Environment

This section loads the packages used for data preparation, scale construction, statistical modeling, estimated marginal means, and figures.

Load Packages

Show code 
library(tidyverse)  # data manipulation + plotting
library(psych)      # scale construction + reliability
library(afex)       # ANOVA models + effect sizes
library(emmeans)    # estimated marginal means + confidence intervals

Data Source and Analysis Dataset

The dataset was imported from the project data folder. The imported dataset was saved as study_raw so that the original file remained unchanged throughout the report.

A smaller analysis dataset was then created for the current analyses. This dataset retained the study condition variables, demographic variables, perceived credibility items, need for cognition items, and trust in science and scientists items needed for variable preparation and analysis.

Variable Preparation

This section prepares the variables used in the primary analyses. The original imported dataset was left unchanged; all prepared variables were created in the working analysis dataset, study_data.

Prepare Participant ID and Experimental Condition

Show code 
study_data <- study_data %>%
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    condition = factor(
      condition,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Low Prestige", "High Prestige")
    )
  )

The experimental condition variable was recoded as a labeled factor with two levels: High Prestige and Low Prestige. A participant ID variable was also created so that each row in the analysis dataset had a unique identifier.

Reverse-Code Scale Items

Items requiring reverse coding were transformed before scale scores were computed. For perceived source credibility, because the items used a 1–7 response scale, reverse-coded items were created by subtracting each original item response from 8. For need for cognition and for trust in science or scientists, because the items used a 1-5 response scale, reverse-coded items were created by subtracting each original item response from 6.

Show code 
study_data <- study_data %>%
  mutate(
    SCSIntelligent_R = 8 - SCSIntelligent,
    SCSHonest_R = 8 - SCSHonest,
    SCSHonorable_R = 8 - SCSHonorable,
    SCSInformed_R = 8 - SCSInformed,
    SCSMoral_R = 8 - SCSMoral,
    SCSbright_R = 8 - SCSbright,
    
    NFC_3_R = 6 - NFC_3,
    NFC_4_R = 6 - NFC_4,
    
    TIS_1_R = 6 - TIS_1,
    TIS_2_R = 6 - TIS_2,
    TIS_3_R = 6 - TIS_3,
    TIS_4_R = 6 - TIS_4,
    TIS_6_R = 6 - TIS_6,
    TIS_8_R = 6 - TIS_8,
    TIS_13_R = 6 - TIS_13,
    TIS_17_R = 6 - TIS_17,
    TIS_18_R = 6 - TIS_18,
    TIS_19_R = 6 - TIS_19,
    TIS_20_R = 6 - TIS_20,
    TIS_21_R = 6 - TIS_21
  )

Create Scale Scores

Scale item lists were defined and used to compute perceived source credibility, need for cognition, and trust in science scores.

Show code 
# Define Source Credibility Scale items: total score
source_total_items <- c(
"SCSIntelligent_R", "SCSTrained", "SCSExpert",
  "SCSInformed_R", "SCSCompetent", "SCSbright_R","SCSSelf", "SCSsensitive", "SCSunderstanding","SCSHonest_R", "SCSTrust", "SCSHonorable_R",
  "SCSMoral_R", "SCSgenuine"
)

# Define Source Credibility Scale items: competence subscale
source_competence_items <- c(
  "SCSIntelligent_R", "SCSTrained", "SCSExpert",
  "SCSInformed_R", "SCSCompetent", "SCSbright_R"
)

# Define Source Credibility Scale items: caring/goodwill subscale
source_goodwill_items <- c(
  "SCSSelf", "SCSsensitive", "SCSunderstanding"
)

# Define Source Credibility Scale items: trustworthiness subscale
source_trustworthiness_items <- c(
  "SCSHonest_R", "SCSTrust", "SCSHonorable_R",
  "SCSMoral_R", "SCSgenuine"
)

# Define Need for Cognition Scale items
nfc_items <- c(
  "NFC_1", "NFC_2", "NFC_3_R",
  "NFC_4_R", "NFC_5", "NFC_6"
)

# Define Trust in Science Scale items
tis_items <- c(
  "TIS_1_R", "TIS_2_R", "TIS_3_R", "TIS_4_R",
  "TIS_5", "TIS_6_R", "TIS_7", "TIS_8_R",
  "TIS_9", "TIS_10", "TIS_11", "TIS_12",
  "TIS_13_R", "TIS_14", "TIS_15", "TIS_16",
  "TIS_17_R", "TIS_18_R", "TIS_19_R",
  "TIS_20_R", "TIS_21_R"
)

# Create scale scores
study_data <- study_data %>%
  mutate(
    source_total_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_total_items)),na.rm = TRUE),
    source_competence_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_competence_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    source_goodwill_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_goodwill_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    source_trustworthiness_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_trustworthiness_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    nfc_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(nfc_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    tis_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(tis_items)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

Create Median Splits

Low/high NFC and TIS grouping variables were created for the two planned 2 × 2 ANOVA models. Participants with scores at or below the sample medians were assigned to the Low level, and participants above the sample medians were assigned to the High level.

Show code 
# Compute median Need for Cognition score
nfc_median <- median(study_data$nfc_scale, na.rm = TRUE)

# Compute median Trust in Science score
tis_median <- median(study_data$tis_scale, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create low/high median split groups
study_data <- study_data %>%
  mutate(
    nfc_msplit = if_else(nfc_scale <= nfc_median, "Low", "High"),
    nfc_msplit = factor(nfc_msplit, levels = c("Low", "High")),
    
    tis_msplit = if_else(tis_scale <= tis_median, "Low", "High"),
    tis_msplit = factor(tis_msplit, levels = c("Low", "High"))
  )

# Print medians
nfc_median
[1] 3.166667

[1] 3.571429

Check Scale Reliability

Internal consistency was estimated for the source credibility, need for cognition, and trust in science scales before the scale scores were used in the primary analyses.

Show code 
# Create item-only data frames for each multi-item rating scale
source_total_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_competence_items))

source_competence_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_competence_items))

source_goodwill_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_goodwill_items))

source_trustworthiness_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_trustworthiness_items))

nfc_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(nfc_items))

tis_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(tis_items))

# Compute internal consistency estimates
source_total_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_total_item_df)
source_total_omega <- psych::omega(source_total_item_df, plot = FALSE)


source_competence_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_competence_item_df)
source_competence_omega <- psych::omega(source_competence_item_df, plot = FALSE)

source_goodwill_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_goodwill_item_df)
source_goodwill_omega <- psych::omega(source_goodwill_item_df, plot = FALSE)

source_trustworthiness_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_trustworthiness_item_df)
source_trustworthiness_omega <- psych::omega(source_trustworthiness_item_df, plot = FALSE)

nfc_alpha <- psych::alpha(nfc_item_df)
nfc_omega <- psych::omega(nfc_item_df, plot = FALSE)

tis_alpha <- psych::alpha(tis_item_df)
tis_omega <- psych::omega(tis_item_df, plot = FALSE)

# Print only alpha and omega coefficients
tibble(
  scale = c(
    "Source Credibility: Total", 
    "Source Credibility: Competence",
    "Source Credibility: Caring/Goodwill",
    "Source Credibility: Trustworthiness",
    "Need for Cognition",
    "Trust in Science"
  ),
  alpha = c(
    source_total_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    source_competence_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    source_goodwill_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    source_trustworthiness_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    nfc_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    tis_alpha$total$raw_alpha
  ),
  omega = c(
    source_total_omega$omega.tot,
    source_competence_omega$omega.tot,
    source_goodwill_omega$omega.tot,
    source_trustworthiness_omega$omega.tot,
    nfc_omega$omega.tot,
    tis_omega$omega.tot
  )
) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
scale alpha omega
Source Credibility: Total 0.67 0.88
Source Credibility: Competence 0.67 0.88
Source Credibility: Caring/Goodwill 0.53 0.58
Source Credibility: Trustworthiness 0.55 0.82
Need for Cognition 0.76 0.89
Trust in Science 0.92 0.94

The reliability table reports Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega for each scale used in the analysis.

These tables report the number and percentages of participants in each age group and gender category.

Primary Analyses

This section reports the primary analyses used to test whether university prestige and the moderators (NFC and TIS) predicted perceived credibility ratings of university research, and the interactions of each moderator with university prestige.

Two 2 x 2 ANOVAs were estimated. Both used perceived credibility of university research as the dependent variable. University prestige was the manipulated independent variable in each ANOVA. The first used NFC as the moderator; the second used TIS as the moderator.

Model 1: Source Total Model with NFC

A 2 x 2 ANOVA tested whether ratings of perceived credibility of university research differed by university prestige, NFC, and university prestige x NFC interaction.

Show code 
#| label: anova_source_total_nfc
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

a1_total <- afex::aov_ez(
  id = "id",
  dv = "source_total_scale",
  between = c("condition", "nfc_msplit"),
  data = study_data
)

# Print the ANOVA table
a1_total
Anova Table (Type 3 tests)

Response: source_total_scale
                Effect    df  MSE    F   ges p.value
1            condition 1, 51 0.54 0.49  .009    .488
2           nfc_msplit 1, 51 0.54 0.00 <.001    .973
3 condition:nfc_msplit 1, 51 0.54 0.02 <.001    .881
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '+' 0.1 ' ' 1

The ANOVA table reports the main effects of university prestige and NFC, and the university prestige x NFC interaction for perceived credibility ratings of research.

Figures

This section creates the figures used to visualize the primary 2 × 2 ANOVA results. The figures are based on the estimated cell means from the two ANOVA models using NFC (Figure 1) and TIS (Figure 5) moderators. Also shown are figures based on the estimated cell means from the two ANOVA models using the three subscale components (competence, goodwill, and trustworthiness) of overall perceived credibility.

Plot 1: Source Total x NFC Interaction Plot

Show code 
p_source_total_nfc_bar <- ggplot(
  as.data.frame(emmeans(a1_total, ~ condition * nfc_msplit)),
  aes(
    x = condition,
    y = emmean,
    fill = nfc_msplit
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
    width = 0.55,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Prestige Condition",
    y = "Mean Source Total Score",
    fill = "Need for Cognition Group"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Low" = "#E76F51", # YOU CAN CHANGE THESE HEX VALUES TO MATCH YOUR POSTER!
      "High" = "#2A9D8F"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 7, 1)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(1, 7)
  ) +
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 14
  )

p_source_total_nfc_bar

This figure shows estimated perceived credibility scores by university prestige and NFC condition. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals.

Results Summary

This section reports the primary analyses used to test whether university prestige level, the need for cognition condition, and their interaction predicted perceived credibility ratings.

It also reports whether university prestige level, the trust in science and scientists level, and their interaction predicted perceived credibility ratings.

Across both ANOVA models, there were no statistically significant main effects or interaction effects. University prestige level was not a statistically significant predictor of perceived credibility ratings. Participants in the high NFC group did not report higher perceived credibility in university research than participants in the low NFC group. Similarly, participants high in trust in science and scientists did not report higher perceived credibility in university research than participants in the low TIS group.

In summary, there was no significant interaction between university prestige and either the NFC level or the TIS level. This indicates that the difference between high and low NFC, and the difference between high and low TIS, did not meaningfully vary across university prestige level.

The estimated means and interaction plots above provide the full model output and visualize the null pattern of results for each outcome.

# About This Report

## About This Report

This reproducible report documents the data preparation, variable construction, descriptive statistics, primary analyses, and figures for this study.

The report is intended to accompany a manuscript-style research paper. It is not the full paper itself. Instead, it shows how the reported analyses were produced from the dataset using a transparent and reproducible Quarto workflow.

## Study Overview

This study examined whether a university’s name influenced perceived credibility of the university’s research on a health topic, and whether credibility ratings differed by need for cognition (NFC), trust in science and scientists (TIS), and their interactions with university prestige.

Two 2 x 2 between-subjects factorial ANOVAs used university prestige as the manipulated independent variable in both analyses. Each ANOVA manipulated a different categorical moderator:

-   Need for Cognition:  high versus low

-   Trust in Science and Scientists:  high versus low.

The dependent variable was the perceived source credibility rating.

The primary analyses tested whether the main effect of university prestige and the particular moderators, NFC or TIS, and whether each moderator’s interaction with university prestige, predicted each source credibility outcome.

### Reverse-Code Scale Items

Items requiring reverse coding were transformed before scale scores were computed. For perceived source credibility, because the items used a 1–7 response scale, reverse-coded items were created by subtracting each original item response from 8. For need for cognition and for trust in science or scientists, because the items used a 1-5 response scale, reverse-coded items were created by subtracting each original item response from 6.

```{r}
#| label: reverse_code_items
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

study_data <- study_data %>%
  mutate(
    SCSIntelligent_R = 8 - SCSIntelligent,
    SCSHonest_R = 8 - SCSHonest,
    SCSHonorable_R = 8 - SCSHonorable,
    SCSInformed_R = 8 - SCSInformed,
    SCSMoral_R = 8 - SCSMoral,
    SCSbright_R = 8 - SCSbright,
    
    NFC_3_R = 6 - NFC_3,
    NFC_4_R = 6 - NFC_4,
    
    TIS_1_R = 6 - TIS_1,
    TIS_2_R = 6 - TIS_2,
    TIS_3_R = 6 - TIS_3,
    TIS_4_R = 6 - TIS_4,
    TIS_6_R = 6 - TIS_6,
    TIS_8_R = 6 - TIS_8,
    TIS_13_R = 6 - TIS_13,
    TIS_17_R = 6 - TIS_17,
    TIS_18_R = 6 - TIS_18,
    TIS_19_R = 6 - TIS_19,
    TIS_20_R = 6 - TIS_20,
    TIS_21_R = 6 - TIS_21
  )
```

### Check Reverse Coding

```{r}
#| label: check_reverse_coding
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

study_data %>%
  select(
    SCSIntelligent, SCSIntelligent_R,
    NFC_3, NFC_3_R,
    TIS_1, TIS_1_R
  ) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

The reverse-coding check shows examples of original and reverse-coded item pairs. These checks confirm that reverse-coded variables were created before scale scores were computed.

### Create Scale Scores

Scale item lists were defined and used to compute perceived source credibility, need for cognition, and trust in science scores.

```{r}
#| label: create_scale_scores
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Define Source Credibility Scale items: total score
source_total_items <- c(
"SCSIntelligent_R", "SCSTrained", "SCSExpert",
  "SCSInformed_R", "SCSCompetent", "SCSbright_R","SCSSelf", "SCSsensitive", "SCSunderstanding","SCSHonest_R", "SCSTrust", "SCSHonorable_R",
  "SCSMoral_R", "SCSgenuine"
)

# Define Source Credibility Scale items: competence subscale
source_competence_items <- c(
  "SCSIntelligent_R", "SCSTrained", "SCSExpert",
  "SCSInformed_R", "SCSCompetent", "SCSbright_R"
)

# Define Source Credibility Scale items: caring/goodwill subscale
source_goodwill_items <- c(
  "SCSSelf", "SCSsensitive", "SCSunderstanding"
)

# Define Source Credibility Scale items: trustworthiness subscale
source_trustworthiness_items <- c(
  "SCSHonest_R", "SCSTrust", "SCSHonorable_R",
  "SCSMoral_R", "SCSgenuine"
)

# Define Need for Cognition Scale items
nfc_items <- c(
  "NFC_1", "NFC_2", "NFC_3_R",
  "NFC_4_R", "NFC_5", "NFC_6"
)

# Define Trust in Science Scale items
tis_items <- c(
  "TIS_1_R", "TIS_2_R", "TIS_3_R", "TIS_4_R",
  "TIS_5", "TIS_6_R", "TIS_7", "TIS_8_R",
  "TIS_9", "TIS_10", "TIS_11", "TIS_12",
  "TIS_13_R", "TIS_14", "TIS_15", "TIS_16",
  "TIS_17_R", "TIS_18_R", "TIS_19_R",
  "TIS_20_R", "TIS_21_R"
)

# Create scale scores
study_data <- study_data %>%
  mutate(
    source_total_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_total_items)),na.rm = TRUE),
    source_competence_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_competence_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    source_goodwill_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_goodwill_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    source_trustworthiness_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(source_trustworthiness_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    nfc_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(nfc_items)), na.rm = TRUE),
    tis_scale = rowMeans(across(all_of(tis_items)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### Check Scale Scores

```{r}
#| label: check_scale_scores
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

study_data %>%
  select(
    source_total_scale,
    
    source_competence_scale,
    source_goodwill_scale,
    source_trustworthiness_scale,
    nfc_scale,
    tis_scale
  ) %>%
  summary()

study_data %>%
  summarise(
    source_total_scale_missing = mean(is.na(source_total_scale)),
    
    source_competence_scale_missing = mean(is.na(source_competence_scale)),
    source_goodwill_scale_missing = mean(is.na(source_goodwill_scale)),
    source_trustworthiness_scale_missing = mean(is.na(source_trustworthiness_scale)),
    nfc_scale_missing = mean(is.na(nfc_scale)),
    tis_scale_missing = mean(is.na(tis_scale))
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

The scale-score checks confirm that the computed scale scores fall within the expected response range and show whether any scale scores are missing.

### Create Median Splits

Low/high NFC and TIS grouping variables were created for the two planned 2 × 2 ANOVA models. Participants with scores at or below the sample medians were assigned to the Low level, and participants above the sample medians were assigned to the High level.

```{r}
#| label: create_median_split_groups
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Compute median Need for Cognition score
nfc_median <- median(study_data$nfc_scale, na.rm = TRUE)

# Compute median Trust in Science score
tis_median <- median(study_data$tis_scale, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create low/high median split groups
study_data <- study_data %>%
  mutate(
    nfc_msplit = if_else(nfc_scale <= nfc_median, "Low", "High"),
    nfc_msplit = factor(nfc_msplit, levels = c("Low", "High")),
    
    tis_msplit = if_else(tis_scale <= tis_median, "Low", "High"),
    tis_msplit = factor(tis_msplit, levels = c("Low", "High"))
  )

# Print medians
nfc_median
tis_median

# Check group sizes
study_data %>%
  count(nfc_msplit) %>%
  knitr::kable()

study_data %>%
  count(tis_msplit) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Median splits created the need for cognition and trust in science moderators used in the primary analyses. The output reports the median values used for the splits and the number of participants assigned to each moderator group.

### Check Scale Reliability

Internal consistency was estimated for the source credibility, need for cognition, and trust in science scales before the scale scores were used in the primary analyses.

```{r}
#| label: check_scale_reliability
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Create item-only data frames for each multi-item rating scale
source_total_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_competence_items))

source_competence_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_competence_items))

source_goodwill_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_goodwill_items))

source_trustworthiness_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(source_trustworthiness_items))

nfc_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(nfc_items))

tis_item_df <- study_data %>% 
  select(all_of(tis_items))

# Compute internal consistency estimates
source_total_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_total_item_df)
source_total_omega <- psych::omega(source_total_item_df, plot = FALSE)


source_competence_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_competence_item_df)
source_competence_omega <- psych::omega(source_competence_item_df, plot = FALSE)

source_goodwill_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_goodwill_item_df)
source_goodwill_omega <- psych::omega(source_goodwill_item_df, plot = FALSE)

source_trustworthiness_alpha <- psych::alpha(source_trustworthiness_item_df)
source_trustworthiness_omega <- psych::omega(source_trustworthiness_item_df, plot = FALSE)

nfc_alpha <- psych::alpha(nfc_item_df)
nfc_omega <- psych::omega(nfc_item_df, plot = FALSE)

tis_alpha <- psych::alpha(tis_item_df)
tis_omega <- psych::omega(tis_item_df, plot = FALSE)

# Print only alpha and omega coefficients
tibble(
  scale = c(
    "Source Credibility: Total", 
    "Source Credibility: Competence",
    "Source Credibility: Caring/Goodwill",
    "Source Credibility: Trustworthiness",
    "Need for Cognition",
    "Trust in Science"
  ),
  alpha = c(
    source_total_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    source_competence_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    source_goodwill_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    source_trustworthiness_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    nfc_alpha$total$raw_alpha,
    tis_alpha$total$raw_alpha
  ),
  omega = c(
    source_total_omega$omega.tot,
    source_competence_omega$omega.tot,
    source_goodwill_omega$omega.tot,
    source_trustworthiness_omega$omega.tot,
    nfc_omega$omega.tot,
    tis_omega$omega.tot
  )
) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The reliability table reports Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega for each scale used in the analysis.

## Primary Analyses

This section reports the primary analyses used to test whether university prestige and the moderators (NFC and TIS) predicted perceived credibility ratings of university research, and the interactions of each moderator with university prestige.

Two 2 x 2 ANOVAs were estimated. Both used perceived credibility of university research as the dependent variable. University prestige was the manipulated independent variable in each ANOVA. The first used NFC as the moderator; the second used TIS as the moderator.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Model 1: Source Total Model with NFC

A 2 x 2 ANOVA tested whether ratings of perceived credibility of university research differed by university prestige, NFC, and university prestige x NFC interaction.

```{r}
#| label: anova_source_total_nfc
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

a1_total <- afex::aov_ez(
  id = "id",
  dv = "source_total_scale",
  between = c("condition", "nfc_msplit"),
  data = study_data
)

# Print the ANOVA table
a1_total
```

The ANOVA table reports the main effects of university prestige and NFC, and the university prestige x NFC interaction for perceived credibility ratings of research.

### Model 1: Estimated Means for Source Total with NFC

```{r}
#| label: estimated_means_source_total_nfc
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

emmeans(a1_total, ~ condition)

emmeans(a1_total, ~ nfc_msplit)

emmeans(a1_total, ~ condition * nfc_msplit)

```

The estimated means show the percieved credibility (null score pattern) across NFC, and the lack of university prestige and NFC interaction.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Figures

This section creates the figures used to visualize the primary 2 × 2 ANOVA results. The figures are based on the estimated cell means from the two ANOVA models using NFC (Figure 1) and TIS (Figure 5) moderators. Also shown are figures based on the estimated cell means from the two ANOVA models using the three subscale components (competence, goodwill, and trustworthiness) of overall perceived credibility.

### Plot 1: Source Total x NFC Interaction Plot

```{r}
#| label: source_total_nfc_interaction_plot
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false

p_source_total_nfc_bar <- ggplot(
  as.data.frame(emmeans(a1_total, ~ condition * nfc_msplit)),
  aes(
    x = condition,
    y = emmean,
    fill = nfc_msplit
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
    width = 0.55,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Prestige Condition",
    y = "Mean Source Total Score",
    fill = "Need for Cognition Group"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Low" = "#E76F51", # YOU CAN CHANGE THESE HEX VALUES TO MATCH YOUR POSTER!
      "High" = "#2A9D8F"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 7, 1)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(1, 7)
  ) +
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 14
  )

p_source_total_nfc_bar
```

This figure shows estimated perceived credibility scores by university prestige and NFC condition. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals.

```{r}
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
```

```{r}
    y = "Mean Source Goodwill Score",
    fill = "Trust in Science Group"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Low" = "#E76F51",
      "High" = "#2A9D8F"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 7, 1)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(1, 7)
  ) +
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 14
  )

p_source_goodwill_tis_bar
```

This figure shows estimated scores of **perceived source goodwill,** **a subscale of overall perceived source credibility**, university prestige, and TIS condition. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals.

## Results Summary

This section reports the primary analyses used to test whether university prestige level, the need for cognition condition, and their interaction predicted perceived credibility ratings.

It also reports whether university prestige level, the trust in science and scientists level, and their interaction predicted perceived credibility ratings.

Across both ANOVA models, there were no statistically significant main effects or interaction effects. University prestige level was not a statistically significant predictor of perceived credibility ratings. Participants in the high NFC group did not report higher perceived credibility in university research than participants in the low NFC group. Similarly, participants high in trust in science and scientists did not report higher perceived credibility in university research than participants in the low TIS group.

In summary, there was no significant interaction between university prestige and either the NFC level or the TIS level. This indicates that the difference between high and low NFC, and the difference between high and low TIS, did not meaningfully vary across university prestige level.

The estimated means and interaction plots above provide the full model output and visualize the null pattern of results for each outcome.
